content.title: About
content.content: Doughnut NFS (2824) is a classic fried sweet pastry shaped as a ring and finished with glaze or sprinkles. It is made from wheat flour, sugar, eggs, milk and yeast, then deep‑fried until golden and coated with sugar glaze, chocolate or various toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Doughnuts appeared in Europe in the 17th century and quickly became popular street food.
In the United States they are called "donuts" and can be ring‑shaped or filled with jam, custard, or cream.
There are over 100 glaze and topping variations, from classic sugar to bright candy crumbs.
In Japan, doughnuts often contain a sweet red‑bean paste (anko) filling.
Doughnuts are commonly paired with coffee as a traditional breakfast.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The carbohydrates in doughnuts are rapidly digested, providing an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the recipe contribute a modest amount of animal protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast and whole‑grain flour (when used) can supply B1, B2 and niacin.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Trans and saturated fats
items.content: Deep‑frying adds trans‑fatty acids and saturated fats, which are unfavorable for heart health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, making doughnuts unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single medium doughnut can contain 250–350 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Doughnuts are usually enjoyed as a dessert or snack, often with coffee or tea. They can be split and filled with cream, jam, or custard. For a lighter option, choose unglazed or lightly topped versions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store doughnuts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag and reheat in the oven before serving.
